<p>“Yeah, Yu-na, I don’t think I can make it today… Na-hyeon’s not feeling well. You ask if she’s sick?”</p><p>I turned my head toward the bed, where Na-hyeon was shaking her head side to side with a pale face.</p><p>She probably wanted me to hide the fact that she was suffering from a hangover after drinking way too much.</p><p>Not a chance.</p><p>“Why? Because she chugged a ton of alcohol at the company dinner last night and now she’s basically a corpse from the hangover.”</p><p>Na-hyeon glared at me for a moment, but she didn’t have the energy to argue and just groaned before closing her eyes.</p><p>“Okay, then see you the day after tomorrow. Love you too.”</p><p>Originally, I was supposed to meet up with Yu-na and Ji-hyeon to go sightseeing on my day off, but Na-hyeon’s binge-drinking had ruined those plans.</p><p>Of course, Yu-na and Ji-hyeon would probably go out and have fun as planned, but given Na-hyeon’s state, I figured I should stick around for at least a day.</p><p>“Ugh… my head… hurts…”</p><p>“So… when I was cleaning this room by myself yesterday, I found eight beer cans rolling around on the floor. Fine, I get the ones from the company dinner, but did you really drink eight cans *alone* in this room?”</p><p>“Don’t scold me… I’ll just get yelled at by Mom the day after tomorrow anyway…”</p><p><img src="data:image/webp;base64," alt="290891" loading="lazy">
</p><p>Seeing Na-hyeon so deflated was kind of cute and amusing.</p><p>“Think of this as punishment for failing to control your desires.”</p><p>“…”</p><p>Na-hyeon didn’t even have the strength to retort—she just kept her eyes shut.</p><p>‘We’ve eaten, so now all that’s left is to put her to sleep…’</p><p>Luckily, when I asked the hotel, a Hunter Association staff member brought me some hangover relief medicine.</p><p>Na-hyeon would probably feel better after a nap… Today was supposed to be a day off for family travel, but the whole day had been wasted.</p><p>Maybe the 9-night, 10-day Tokyo trip was too long—Yu-na and Ji-hyeon had only gone all out for the first two days before switching to a more relaxed schedule.</p><p>When I went to the hotel lobby to get the hangover medicine, I saw Se-rin dressed in a suit, heading somewhere.</p><p>I’d considered killing time with her, but she just gave me a quick greeting before hurrying off, so she must have work today too.</p><p>‘There was a café on the first floor… maybe I should just pass the time there…’</p><p>***</p><p>I was sitting alone in the café on the first floor of the hotel, sipping the coffee I’d ordered.</p><p>The staff were Japanese, so I was a little worried, but they had a Korean menu and were kind enough that I managed to point and order.</p><p>‘Without Na-hyeon, I’m basically an international lost child…’</p><p>Since it was a day off, everyone else must have gone out sightseeing—because the café was empty except for me, sitting alone by the window, slowly drinking my coffee.</p><p>‘Well… it’s nice to have a day like this once in a while…’</p><p>“Ah, thank god!”</p><p>Just then, a voice I hadn’t heard in a while—but was all too familiar—came from the café entrance.</p><p>“Ah.”</p><p>Standing at the door was Kang Hye-na, my oldest friend and the only Hunter Training Academy alumni I still kept in touch with.</p><p>As soon as she saw me, she grinned from ear to ear, waving her hand as she strode over.</p><p>‘Why is she so worked up…’</p><p>“Hey, Yoon Seong-hyeon! How could you not contact me once since you got here?”</p><p><img src="data:image/webp;base64," alt="290892" loading="lazy">
</p><p>“I figured I’d see you when I arrived, but you weren’t around?”</p><p>“Forget that. Actually, this works out perfectly. Can you spare me one, two, maybe three hours?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“You didn’t even hear what I need.”</p><p>As expected… Even after meeting so many people as a Hunter—even sleeping with some of them—no one was as easy to talk to as Hye-na.</p><p>I had no idea what she wanted help with, but the mere thought of it was already exhausting, so I rejected her outright.</p><p>Hye-na pouted slightly before speaking.</p><p>“I was the one who arranged for your sister to come here with you, right? And don’t forget, Hunter Yoon Seong-hyeon, you’ve been getting all the good job leads through me.”</p><p>“Fine, I’ll at least hear you out.”</p><p>Hye-na had pulled the Yoon Na-hyeon card the second I refused. But it wasn’t like she was lying—thanks to her, Na-hyeon had been able to come here with me. So, I decided to at least listen to what she had to say.</p><p>“Today, we’re supposed to have a sparring session with some people from the Japanese Hunter Association as a goodwill gesture. But one of our Hunters got wasted on Dropz last night and passed out. Can you fill in for him?”</p><p>“You want me to fight a Japanese Hunter…?”</p><p>“It’s not a fight, just sparring. No one’s getting hurt.”</p><p>“Ugh…”</p><p>I let out a sigh. Not because the request was unreasonable, but because it was so trivial.</p><p>If it were something dangerous, I could at least reject it outright. But a friendly sparring match with the Japanese Association? That was harder to turn down.</p><p>Sparring was never serious anyway. It was just a few exchanges, then someone called it, they shook hands, and that was that.</p><p>Considering all the favors Hye-na had done for me, I couldn’t exactly say no.</p><p>“Why don’t you go instead?”</p><p>“I already asked, but the director chewed me out—why would I go to something like that? Plus, if I went, they’d expect someone of equal rank, and I don’t think they’d appreciate that.”</p><p>“Who’s the Japanese Hunter that was supposed to spar with the drunk?”</p><p>“No idea. Just some A-rank Hunter who recently got promoted. That’s why I thought if we sent you—another newly promoted A-rank—they’d understand. The Association’s been looking for someone, but it’s a rest day, so everyone’s MIA.”</p><p>“Fine… But if it goes past three hours, I’m leaving.”</p><p>“It’ll be over fast, don’t worry.”</p><p>I accepted the request, thinking it might be nice to stretch my legs a little. The opponent probably wouldn’t take it seriously either, and even if the sparring got intense, I could just play along and throw the match when the time was right.</p><p>‘If I mess up there, things might get even more annoying later…’</p><p>“Hurry up and come out. The car’s waiting in front, so we’ll head straight to the Association’s underground training hall.”</p><p>“Okay.”</p><p>Kang Hye-na stepped out of the café, humming with a look of relief on her face.</p><p>‘But… Hye-na’s grown up, huh. She used to act like such a kid back then.’</p><p>***</p><p>The location was an underground training hall a short distance from the Association’s main building where we worked.</p><p>I had no idea whether we copied them, they copied us, or if there was some kind of standard, but the Korean Association’s training hall and this one were shockingly similar.</p><p>No—similar didn’t even cover it. They were practically identical. The only difference was the sparring gear provided by the Association.</p><p>While Korea’s was a plain black design, here they came in various colors. The style was lighter, too—something you could wear for regular exercise.</p><p>Each country had selected five Hunters—either those who had recently reached A-rank or were on the lower end of the A-rank spectrum—to compete in one-on-one matches.</p><p>At first, the atmosphere had been friendly, but…</p><p>For some reason, starting from the second match, Hunters from both countries had begun hurling trash talk at each other, and the tension had only escalated from there. Han Ji-hyeok and the Japanese Association President’s expressions had grown serious.</p><p>By the third match, blood was literally splattering across the floor. Then again, these were Hunters—none of them batted an eye at a little blood. The referee, who had been quick to intervene at the start, now just stood by and watched until one fighter went down.</p><p>The atmosphere had shifted entirely—like MMA fighters brawling in the Octagon while the crowd roared in excitement.</p><p>The current score was 2-2. The final match would decide the winner of this “friendly” exchange. And the worst part? I was the last one up.</p><p>“Then, the next participant—ah, I mean, the next Hunter for the match, Yoon Seong-hyeon, please step forward.”</p><p>Even the interpreter, who wasn’t even part of the Association, called my name with a gleam in his eyes, as if to say, ‘You’ve got this.’</p><p>The Japanese side’s final contestant was a towering figure—easily two meters tall, with a hulking, muscular frame. His tanned skin, blonde hair, and the grotesque golden sun tattoos covering his entire body made him look less like a Hunter and more like…</p><p>‘Is he even a Hunter? Looks like a yakuza.’</p><p>I turned my head toward the VIP seats where the Association Presidents were seated. The Japanese President nodded at the golden sun, while Han Ji-hyeok looked at me, clenched his fists, and struck a fighting pose.</p><p>The mood was now indistinguishable from the finals of a Korea vs. Japan showdown.</p><p>‘At this point, I can’t even pretend to lose…’</p><p>Maybe I should make it look like a close fight before pulling out the win.</p><p>It might sound arrogant, but I didn’t think I’d lose to that hulking golden sun.</p><p>“Then, please shake hands—Kunimoto Taichi and Yoon Seong-hyeon.”</p><p>Now they were outright calling us “athletes,” and no one even batted an eye.</p><p>The mountain of a man named Kunimoto Taichi grinned widely and extended his hand toward me.</p><p>As soon as our hands touched, Geum Taeyang suddenly seemed to remember something. He looked at me and began muttering in Japanese with a grin.</p><p>“What’s he saying?”</p><p>“Uh… that…”</p><p>“Is he cursing at me?”</p><p>“No, it’s not that… He’s talking about someone Yoon Seong-hyeon knows… He said he saw the two of them eating together…”</p><p>He must have seen Ji-hyeon and me eating at the Japanese Association’s cafeteria.</p><p>But the Japanese interpreter and Geum Taeyang started snickering in a way that made my skin crawl. Even if I didn’t understand the language, I could tell the tone they were using to talk about me.</p><p>“Is that really all he said?”</p><p>“No…”</p><p>“Then just tell me everything.”</p><p>“Should I… paraphrase it a little?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Ahem… Well…”</p><p>The interpreter made up his mind and spoke. “He said, ‘Isn’t that the guy who was with that hot bitch? She looked like his girlfriend, but if I fold him in half here, I’d feel bad. Just thinking about it gets me excited again.’”</p><p>‘So he’s rotten to the core, not just on the outside.’</p><p>The Japanese interpreter seemed to tell Geum Taeyang that our interpreter had just translated his vulgar remarks to me.</p><p>But instead of looking flustered, Geum Taeyang just burst into laughter and returned to his seat.</p><p>“Alright, then Yang, get ready…”</p><p>If he had just cursed at me, I could have laughed it off. But the moment he dragged my family into this, Geum Taeyang had crossed the line.</p><p>My fists clenched, and I felt my lips trembling.</p><p>“Start!”</p><p>The moment the signal came, I pushed off the ground and lunged straight for Geum Taeyang. He must have expected a probing attack—he hadn’t even raised the training two-handed sword in his grip, his face frozen in shock.</p><p>THUD!</p><p>My fist connected squarely with his solar plexus. A sickening *crack* echoed as a trickle of blood spilled from his lips.</p><p>“Hngh—!”</p><p>CLANG</p><p>Geum Taeyang coughed up blood, dropped his sword, and fell to his knees. Clutching his stomach with both hands, he gasped for air a few times before collapsing unconscious.</p><p>“Huh?”</p><p>“Oh.”</p><p>Silence filled the training hall for a few seconds. Everyone was stunned that the match had ended in under five seconds.</p><p>Then our interpreter rushed over, grabbed my hand, and raised it toward the ceiling. “Yoon Seong-hyeon wins!” he shouted.</p><p>Geum Taeyang was carried out, but fortunately, the Japanese Hunters still applauded me.</p><p>Someone even whistled and cheered as if announcing the birth of a new champion.</p><p>‘What the hell is this?’</p>
